articles.title_orig: House candidate who reported rape on campaign trail on why she came forward: "What about all the women who are victims?"
articles.title_zh: House candidate who reported rape on campaign trail on why she came forward: "What about all the women who are victims?"
articles.content_orig:
In the days since U.S. House candidate Bernadette Greene-Placentia publicly came forward alleging she was raped over the summer while repairing a campaign sign, she says women have been reaching out to her to share their own stories.
"The humbling thing is that so many – hundreds and hundreds of women from around the world — have taken the time to write me and tell me their own story," Greene-Placentia told CBS News in an interview. "I would say about 70% of them have acknowledged that they never reported it, and they are thanking me for being in the public eye and talking about it and giving voice because they didn't feel like they had a voice when they went through the same thing."
Greene-Placentia, a Democrat, is facing freshman Republican Rep. Abe Hamadeh on the ballot in November in Arizona's 8th District, located in the Phoenix suburbs. The district is rated as solidly Republican by Cook Political Report.
The reported sexual assault happened amid a heated campaign season, as concerns about political violence swirl. At a rally in September, an armed man lunged at Ohio gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton, and at a town hall earlier this year, a man lunged and sprayed vinegar at Rep. Ilhan Omar.
Greene-Placentia, who had been a long-haul trucker, told CBS News that "we are not a well-funded campaign," and she and her staff were usually the ones putting up campaign signs or fixing them.
"I took pride in being able to, you know, do these things myself because we are a grassroots campaign, so it wasn't unusual," she said of fixing signs at all hours.
She said that a "little after midnight" one night in August, she was repairing some supplies when she was hit on the back of the head. When she regained consciousness, she said she realized she was on the ground, and a "man was on top of me, and then I felt pain down there." She said that man "climbed off," and then another man assaulted her.
"At that point, I remember I started, like, moving around and kicking," she said. "He said, 'You know, just not worth it.' And they left. I don't know how long I stayed there."
Greene-Placentia said she drove straight home, and she said she believes police have footage of her driving home.
A police report from the Maricopa County Sheriff's Office says the incident occurred on Aug. 14 between 2 a.m. and 3 a.m., and she reported the incident on Aug. 31.
The Maricopa County Sheriff's Office said in a statement earlier this week that it was investigating the incident but could not comment further.
Greene-Placentia said she told her husband and staff the next day, but she didn't want to talk about it at first.
Greene-Placentia said Friday that she realized she wanted to come forward while she was telling her own personal story on the trail. She said she was talking about how her father died while waiting to get care with the Department of Veterans Affairs and she found out six months later that her mother had been rationing her insulin.
"I was asking them, 'Do you think anybody's gonna fight harder than me?'" Greene-Placentia said. "And then in the back of my head, I'm like, 'Well you're telling these folks that you're gonna fight for them, but what about all the women that are victims of sexual assault? Are you not gonna fight for them? That kind of makes you a hypocrite, Bernadette.'"
Greene-Placentia's story was first published on Wednesday in the Phoenix New Times. Since then, her opponent, Hamadeh, called it a "disturbing story," and he was calling "upon authorities to investigate these serious allegations thoroughly, including finding all possible camera footage of the time and place in order to prosecute the crime to the fullest extent of the law."
Greene-Placentia said that she wants to tell women who come up to her that she understands what they are going through.
"As women, we want to take responsibility for everything and blame ourselves, and that is a societal problem we've got to get away from," Greene-Placentia said.

articles.title_orig: Christa Pike discharged from hospital, 10 days after failed execution
articles.title_zh: Christa Pike discharged from hospital, 10 days after failed execution
articles.content_orig:
US death row inmate Christa Pike has been discharged from hospital following her botched execution at the end of last month, her lawyers have said.
Pike, 50, has been sent back to the prison where she has spent the last 30 years and is continuing to receive medical care, according to a statement from her lawyers on Saturday.
She survived two lethal injections of the drug pentobarbital on 30 September, which left her in a critical condition.
Pike regained consciousness earlier this week and began speaking - stunning experts, medical staff and her lawyers.
Her case is now in uncharted territory as she is thought to be the only person to have survived an execution attempt by lethal injection.
I've seen nearly 500 executions - but never one like Christa Pike's
I interviewed Christa Pike 20 years ago - I can't stop thinking about her
What happened in Christa Pike's failed US execution, and how did she survive?
Pike's lawyers said in their statement that she was "grateful to the first responders and her medical team for their care in these extraordinary circumstances".
It is unclear what medical care Pike is receiving now that she is back in prison but her lawyers previously said she faced a "long road to recovery".
The Tennessee Department of Correction is yet to say why the execution did not go as planned, though it has defended the method it used.
How widely used is the death penalty in the US?
At a court hearing on Wednesday, Tennessee Assistant Attorney General Will Ayers told the judge he did not know whether the state intends to try to execute her again.
The judge ordered the state to preserve all evidence related to the failed injections. That evidence could lay the groundwork for a future lawsuit against the state.
Pike was 18 when she and her then-boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, beat, tortured and killed 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, whom they had met at a job training camp for low-income young people.
Shipp was spared the death penalty because he was not legally an adult when the crime was committed. He remains in prison.
Pike was the first woman scheduled to be executed in the state of Tennessee in over 200 years.
Her lawyers have spent decades appealing her case. In the days leading up to her scheduled execution, both the US Supreme Court and Tennessee Governor Bill Lee declined to block the execution.
Since it failed, Pike's lawyers have renewed their calls for her sentence to be commuted to life in prison without the possibility of parole.
Colleen Slemmer was tortured and brutally killed by Pike and Shipp
Pike lost consciousness and was taken to a local hospital following her botched execution. Her legal team believed for days that she was brain dead and expected her to be taken off life support at any moment.
Pike eventually woke up and began talking again on Tuesday - her lawyer Randy Spivey said her first words were "Where am I?" and "Who are you?"
At a press conference on Wednesday, her lawyers said she was shackled to the bed and suffering from pneumonia and significant swelling on her arms, while also being unable to swallow.
"We don't know the toll all of this will take" Spivey said of her mental health, adding that Pike felt "angry and confused".

articles.title_orig: Police officer dies after West Philadelphia shooting; another injured with 12 gunshot wounds
articles.title_zh: Police officer dies after West Philadelphia shooting; another injured with 12 gunshot wounds
articles.content_orig:
Video taken in cities including Paris, Lyon and Strasbourg showed demonstrators facing off with police, lighting fires and dodging tear gas. France’s interior ministry said over 6,000 people had been taken into custody.
French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu defended the police response to student protests after one teenager lost a hand in an incident involving a police grenade and another lost sight in one eye after being struck by a projectile.
In parliament on Tuesday, Lecornu pushed back on accusations of police brutality or state repression, adding that the term "police brutality" implies that officers had been instructed to use force, according to Politico.
"What triggers police action is the occurrence of urban violence," Lecornu said.
"Can accidents happen? The answer is yes," he added.
FRANCE EXPLODES AGAIN AS STUDENTS RIOT OVER EDUCATION
French riot police stand near burning objects during clashes with protesters in Paris on Tuesday, Oct. 6, 2026. (Reuters)
Lecornu and Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez have both argued that the police response was sparked by urban violence, arson and vandalism, while maintaining that officers have acted within their authority. Nuñez also called the police response proportionate in "almost all cases."
The prime minister also accused opposition party France Unbowed of exploiting the student protests to sow chaos and score political points ahead of next year’s presidential election.
President Emmanuel Macron convened an emergency meeting with senior ministers to address the nationwide student protests and their potential political fallout.
The French government is facing mounting pressure after more than 6,500 people were arrested and hundreds were injured as students demand better funding and learning conditions in schools. Most of those arrested were minors, according to The Associated Press.
Riot police use a water cannon as they face students during a protest against under-resourced schools in Rennes, western France, on Tuesday, Oct. 6, 2026. (Jeremias Gonzalez/AP)
Lecornu said 215 students and 85 school staff members had been injured since the protests began, while his office said 715 police officers had also been injured.
"I hope we can provide a political response to a very real anxiety among high school students," Lecornu acknowledged.
As Lecornu delivered his remarks on Tuesday, demonstrators from several French unions and teachers’ groups gathered with high school and university students. Members of France’s left-wing parties were also at the protest, according to Politico.
The Interior Ministry estimated that 266,000 people took part in demonstrations nationwide Tuesday, including 56,000 in Paris.
The Paris demonstration was largely peaceful, although smaller groups later clashed with riot police, according to The Associated Press.
The protesters' movement began at high schools in the Paris region in mid-September before spreading nationwide.
TEEN'S HAND BLOWN OFF BY POLICE GRENADE DURING FRENCH STUDENT PROTESTS: REPORT
French riot police officers remove elements of a burning street barricade during a demonstration by French high school and university students in Lyon on Oct. 6, 2026. (Reuters)

On Monday, a 15-year-old boy in northern France lost a hand after a police grenade exploded during the protests, Politico reported. A prosecutor said he could not "say for certain whether the student picked up the grenade or whether it was thrown at him."
In the city of Tours, a 16-year-old lost sight in one eye after being hit by a projectile, according to the outlet. The prosecutor said the projectile may have been fired from a sub-lethal riot-control weapon used by police.
Boris Vallaud, leader of the center-left Socialist group in parliament, said the group's lawmakers would introduce legislation restricting the use of sub-lethal riot-control weapons at student demonstrations, warning that they can cause irreversible injuries, the outlet reported.

articles.title_orig: Four dead and thousands without power after Hurricane Isaias lashes US
articles.title_zh: Four dead and thousands without power after Hurricane Isaias lashes US
articles.content_orig:
Watch: Florida thrashed as Hurricane Isaias makes landfall
Four people have died and hundreds of thousands are without power after Hurricane Isaias battered parts of the southern US with powerful winds and heavy rain.
Officials reported two deaths each in the states of Alabama and Florida, which included people who were killed when trees fell on their houses.
At least 500,000 people were without power in several states as of Saturday evening, according to tracker PowerOutage.
Isaias made landfall in Florida late on Friday with maximum sustained winds of 105mph (168km/h) before being downgraded to a post-tropical cyclone.
The storm felled trees and ripped the roofs off buildings. Alabama, Florida and Georgia all declared states of emergency ahead of its arrival, while both Florida and Alabama issued mandatory evacuation orders to thousands of people.
Meanwhile, Hurricane Simon is bearing down on Mexico's Pacific coast and has strengthened to category four. It is expected to make landfall sometime overnight.
Tropical Storm Rachel, also in the Pacific Ocean, is expected to hit southern California later on Saturday.
The roof was blown off an apartment complex in Milton, Florida
Two deaths related to Isaias were reported in Florida's Escambia County. A woman was killed when a tree fell on her house, local Sheriff Chip Simmons said.
Joey Williams told NewsNation his wife had died in the storm. He said they went outside to snap pictures of the damage but, when they went back into their home, a tree fell through the roof and trapped them.
"I was able to squeeze out. My wife didn't make it," Williams told the outlet.
Simmons later reported that a man had died from carbon monoxide poisoning after running a generator in a garage that was not properly ventilated. Four other people who were in the same house were taken to hospital.
Officials had to rescue people in vehicles that became submerged by floodwaters. The Florida National Guard shared pictures of a truck stuck in a flood ditch, saying soldiers "stopped, swam to the vehicle and pulled its occupants to safety".
Florida Governor Ron DeSantis said flooding was a continued risk and warned of a "very hazardous situation".
In Florida, the storm tore through houses
The canopy of a petrol station collapsed in Gulf Breeze, Florida
In neighbouring Alabama, a sheriff was injured when a tree fell on him as he was responding to a car crash.
"Unfortunately, we have also learned that two Alabamians have lost their lives," Governor Kay Ivey said in a post on X, without giving further details on the circumstances of the deaths.
She also said officials were concerned about "spinoff tornadoes" in the state from the strong winds and heavy rain.
"As we approach the weekend and any travel plans, make sure you have reliable information as conditions develop," she said.
In Charleston, South Carolina, officials asked people to stay home on Saturday night as high tide is expected to reach 7.5ft (2.3m).
"After dark, floodwater is much harder to see and it's impossible to judge how deep it is from behind the wheel," the city said.
The storm is expected to continue to weaken as it travels to the north-east, but the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (Noaa) warned that the Carolinas and Georgia could see floods from up to 10 inches (25cm) of rainfall.
Hurricane Isaias was the first hurricane in the Atlantic's hurricane season, which largely has been delayed due to El NiÃ±o conditions in the Pacific.

articles.title_orig: How a museum masterpiece’s life-size replica sparked rare US-China collaboration
articles.title_zh: How a museum masterpiece’s life-size replica sparked rare US-China collaboration
articles.content_orig:
Beijing team’s results based on 14th century Yuan dynasty mural hailed for ‘profound historical and practical significance’
For anyone who has visited the Chinese galleries at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York, there is one work that stops them in their tracks.
Stepping into Gallery 206, home to Chinese Buddhist art, visitors are met by a monumental wall – over 15 metres wide and 7.5 metres tall (nearly 50 feet by 25 feet) – covered in a Buddhist assembly so vast and majestic that it momentarily erases the Manhattan bustle outside.
The work left a lasting impression on Zhang Jian, director of the Meticulous Painting Institute at the Chinese National Academy of Arts, who visited the Met three times before 2023.

articles.title_orig: 9 dead in Erie, Pennsylvania, shooting, including gunman
articles.title_zh: 9 dead in Erie, Pennsylvania, shooting, including gunman
articles.content_orig:
A man killed seven family members and a family friend at a home in Erie, Pennsylvania, on Friday night before dying of an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound, officials said.
The victims ranged in age from 22 months to 44 years old and included two children and a pregnant woman, Erie police said.
“It was the worst scene I have ever experienced,” said Police Chief Rick Lorah, who called it horrific.
Police responded to a home just before 5 p.m. on a ShotSpotter alert indicating two gunshots went off, Lorah said at a Saturday news conference.
When officers arrived, they found two women, ages 51 and 37, dead outside of the residence, the chief said.
Lorah said a neighbor’s Ring doorbell video showed those two women “arriving at the residence, appearing distressed, seeking assistance from neighbors and pounding on the door.”
Audio from video reviewed by investigators also “appears to capture muffled gunfire from inside the residence before the suspect emerged and fatally shot both women,” Lorah said.
The suspect then went back inside and witnesses reported hearing no further gunshots, Lorah said.
When officers arrived, they didn’t hear any movement inside the home and were unable to establish contact with anyone, Lorah said, adding it wasn’t clear whether someone was inside and posed a threat.
Ultimately, SWAT officers breached several doors and deployed a robot, which found multiple victims, and officers went in, the chief said.
Investigators determined the victims were killed and the suspect died by a self-inflicted gunshot wound before officers arrived.
Eight of the deceased, including the suspect, were related and one of the two women killed outside was a family friend, Lorah said. One of the victims found inside was eight months pregnant, he added.
“It’s a family,” Lorah said.
Two young children — a 5-year-old boy and a 22-month-old girl — were found on the first floor.
Four victims were found on the second floor in the stairwell: a 24-year-old woman, a 44-year-old woman, a 19-year-old man and a 21-year-old man.
The suspected shooter, 45, who was not publicly identified, was found dead on the second floor. A .40 caliber handgun that was registered to the suspect was recovered “on his person,” Lorah said.
The police chief said all the victims inside the home lived there, and the two women found outside did not.
The investigation into what precipitated the shooting is ongoing.
Lorah said “it’s too soon to talk about motive” but that he believed “mental health is at play here.”
He said investigators will look into what the two women found deceased outside the home knew when they arrived at the scene.
“We have to look at their cellphones. They knew something was going on at that house,” he said.
“We believe that the shooter comes out and calls towards the two females. They run towards and then he, then he shoots them,” Lorah said of the sequence of events.
Gov. Josh Shapiro said he had spoken with Erie Mayor Daria Devlin and offered his administration’s “full support.”
“My heart breaks for this family,” he wrote on X. “Lori and I are praying for their loved ones and the entire Erie community.”
Erie is about 128 miles north of Pittsburgh.
Joe Kottke is an assignment editor at NBC News covering breaking news across the Americas, including politics, immigration, crime and severe weather.
Marlene Lenthang is a breaking news reporter for NBC News Digital.

Several people were wounded in an attack on King Khalid International Airport in Saudi Arabia’s capital Riyadh on Saturday that forced a suspension of operations, the country’s civil aviation authority said.
There was ‌no immediate claim of responsibility for the attack, but it comes amid an escalation of missile strikes by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis against Saudi Arabia.
The airport had already been struck in two earlier attacks this week that left four people dead and exposed vulnerabilities in the kingdom’s ability to defend itself as it wages war on the Houthis. Saudi Arabia’s early warning system did not issue an alert ahead of Saturday’s incident.

articles.title_orig: Hundreds of doctors demand World Medical Association suspend Israel
articles.title_zh: Hundreds of doctors demand World Medical Association suspend Israel
articles.content_orig:
Hundreds of doctors have gathered outside the World Medical Association (WMA) summit in the Netherlands, calling for the suspension of the Israeli Medical Association (IMA) from the grouping of physicians.
On Saturday, 81 healthcare workers removed their scrubs and hung them in a line facing the WMA assembly in Rotterdam, each bearing the name of a Palestinian healthcare worker currently held in illegal Israeli detention.
It was part of a protest against the continued membership of the Israeli association in the WMA, “despite them breaching almost every ethical principle in the WMA’s Code of Medical Ethics”, the IMA Out! coalition that organised the demonstration said in a statement.
“These scrubs should not be empty. Our colleagues belong with their patients, not in Israeli prisons. Today, we literally placed their names at the WMA’s doorstep,” said Mejrem Ahmetaj, a general practitioner and member of IMA Out!.
Since October 2023, Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza has killed more than 1,700 Palestinian healthcare workers and destroyed nearly all the hospitals and healthcare facilities in the enclave.
The campaign accused the Israeli medical association of remaining silent as Palestinian healthcare has been systematically destroyed.
“The IMA is not a bystander. It defends these attacks and blocks international condemnation while Palestinian healthcare is being destroyed. That is not medical neutrality. That is complicity,” added Ahmetaj.
At a meeting of international doctors, medical leaders and human rights activists during the WMA summit on Thursday, the destruction of Palestinian healthcare and the responsibility of the international medical community were discussed, the campaign said.
“Our Palestinian colleagues are being killed and imprisoned, where they are starved and tortured. Their hospitals have been destroyed and patients driven out or murdered. The IMA has said and done nothing about these war crimes against health workers, patients and hospitals,” said a statement by Jonathan Fluxman on behalf of IMA OUT!.
“Thirty years of WMA dialogue with the IMA has done nothing but give the IMA a sense of impunity … It is time for national medical associations and the WMA to speak out and take action. Break your ties with the IMA and suspend the IMA from the WMA now,” he added.
The IMA OUT! campaign said it delivered a petition calling for the IMA’s suspension, signed by more than 6,500 health workers from around the world.
They also demanded accountability for the complicity of Israeli doctors in the starvation, torture and medical neglect of Palestinian prisoners.
Among those held by Israel is Dr Hussam Abu Safia , head of Gaza’s Kamal Adwan Hospital, whose unlawful detention has prompted an international outcry.
He was briefly held at the notorious Sde Teiman detention camp and has been subject to torture and medical neglect. Doctors protesting in Rotterdam held up placards demanding his release.
Abu Safia’s son Elyas, addressing a meeting organised by the campaign, said, “My father and all Palestinian detainees must be treated in accordance with medical ethics, and doctors must abide by the Hippocratic oath they have taken. Care cannot be given based on whose life is deemed worthy.”

articles.title_orig: Protests against voter roll revisions rock capital of world's largest democracy
articles.title_zh: Protests against voter roll revisions rock capital of world's largest democracy
articles.content_orig:
Thousands gather in Mumbai with heavy police presence as concerns mount that millions will be denied voting rights
India’s youth-led Cockroach movement kicked off more nationwide protests on Friday as thousands of people gathered in Mumbai, amid mounting concerns that millions of citizens are being unfairly stripped of their vote.
The movement, which calls itself the Cockroach Janta party (CJP) and has massive support among the country’s gen Zs, returned to the streets to demand the resignation of the chief election commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar.
Kumar has become a highly contentious figure after a report in the Indian Express newspaper alleged irregularities and internal concerns about a process to revise and “purify” India’s electoral register, called the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).
SIR, which was overseen by Kumar, has resulted in tens of millions of people being deleted from the electoral register. Large numbers are challenging their removal.
Opposition politicians and civil society groups have alleged SIR is part of a widespread manipulation of India’s electoral system to benefit the ruling Bharatiya Janata party (BJP).
The CJP began as online satire but grew into a powerful manifestation of youth power and an unexpected challenge to the Narendra Modi government. There were protests for weeks in the heart of Delhi and the education minister was eventually pressured into resigning in July . In the aftermath, the group declared it would remain active as a “pressure group” to hold the government to account on issues of education and democracy.
Last week, after the revelations about the election commission, the CJP’s founder, Abhijeet Dipke, announced that if Kumar did not resign over the controversy, the “Cockroaches” would resume their agitation until he stepped down. Dipke said the Mumbai protest would kick off a nationwide movement, with more protests planned in Delhi, Goa, Kolkata and Bengaluru.
The authorities denied permission for the group to hold their protest at Mumbai’s Shivaji park but Dipke had vowed to go ahead regardless. “We are fighting against those in power,” he said at a press conference. “We all remember Mahatma Gandhi, who fought against the Britishers. Did the British ever permit him to agitate?”
Hundreds of people assembled in Mumbai on Friday afternoon, amid a heavy police presence, including many young people who said they were there to fight for India’s democracy.
“Voting is the most basic right of any citizen, but because of the actions of Kumar and the election commission, that right is under attack,” said Deesha, 22, a student activist. “So many millions of people have lost their votes and aren’t even recognised as citizens of India any more. This attack on our democracy must stop. The first important step is to get Gyanesh Kumar to resign, and then SIR must be reversed.”
Janvi Upadhyay, 18, said the Cockroach movement had awoken the young people of India “and if they think they can just come and take away votes and cheat the elections, we will show them just how wrong they are”.
after newsletter promotion
“We already forced the education minister to resign. Gyanesh Kumar should be very worried right now because he is definitely next,” she said.
The election commission has denied wrongdoing in the SIR but in a move that appeared ​aimed at easing tensions, officials were directed to expedite the process to register newly eligible voters and those who claimed to have been wrongly omitted from electoral rolls.
Anger at Kumar and the election commission also erupted in Delhi on Friday, even as the police took draconian measures to try to stop people from protesting. Thousands of police were deployed to the Jantar Mantar protest site in Delhi – which was the epicentre of the last Cockroach agitation in July – a dozen metro stations in the surrounding area were closed and an internet shutdown was imposed.
Hundreds of those who turned out to Jantar Mantar were immediately forced into police buses. The mass detentions of at least 700 people, including civil society leaders and opposition politicians, prompted outrage, with protesters leaning out of the bus windows to accuse police officers of depriving them of their fundamental democratic rights.
Opposition parties said they would also start a nationwide protest movement to demand Kumar’s resignation. All opposition lawmakers plan to march to the election ​commission office in Delhi next week.

10-year police veteran Shane Seiber was killed after responding to a report of a man with a gun
A Philadelphia police officer was fatally shot and another was wounded on Saturday after responding to a report of a man with a gun, authorities said.
Shane Seiber, 40, was killed early on Saturday morning in West Philadelphia , according to the city’s police commissioner, Kevin Bethel.
Seiber, a 10-year veteran of the Philadelphia police department, and the other officer were transported to the Penn Presbyterian medical center, where the surviving officer underwent surgery. He was listed in stable condition, Bethel said.
Bethel also said a suspect was in custody.
Citing law enforcements sources, the Philadelphia Inquirer identified that suspect as Eric Lewis. The Inquirer also reported that Lewis, 35, was employed by Philadelphia’s municipal water department.
Pennsylvania’s governor, Josh Shapiro, said he ordered flags to fly at half-mast for Seiber. He is survived by his wife and two children: a boy, age seven, and a girl, three.
Seiber was at least the 376th Philadelphia police department officer to die in the line of duty since 1851, according to the Officer Down Memorial Page , which honors US law enforcement personnel who died while on the job. He was the 129th of those officers to die from gunfire, the memorial page said.

articles.title_orig: Care Starts Here: Self-care Strategies for World Mental Health Day
articles.title_zh: Care Starts Here: Self-care Strategies for World Mental Health Day
articles.content_orig:
Every year on Oct. 10, World Mental Health Day invites people around the globe to raise awareness, challenge stigma and advocate for stronger mental health supports. It is also an opportunity to pause and consider a simple but important question: What helps us care for our own mental wellbeing so we can keep showing up for ourselves and one another?
This year, the National Council for Mental Wellbeing is recognizing World Mental Health Day with the theme Care Starts Here . It is a reminder that self-care is not selfish or optional. Small, intentional acts of care can support our mental wellbeing, strengthen our resilience and help us be more present for the people and communities around us.
Mental health is essential to overall health, yet millions of people still face stigma and barriers to support. World Mental Health Day creates space for honest conversations about those challenges while reinforcing a shared truth: mental wellbeing is a collective responsibility. When individuals, workplaces, schools and communities prioritize mental health, they help create environments where people can seek support earlier and move toward recovery and wellbeing.
The observance also reminds us that awareness should lead to action. Action can include advocating for mental health services, checking in with someone we care about and building habits that support our own wellbeing. Care may begin with one person, one conversation or one manageable choice.
Self-care does not have to be elaborate, expensive or perfect. It looks different for everyone and may change from one day to the next. The National Council’s Care Starts Here self-care guide encourages people to begin with one action that feels manageable:
The goal is not to complete a checklist. It is to notice what you need, choose a realistic step and pay attention to how it affects you. A sustainable practice is flexible, connected to your routine and open to change when it no longer helps.
Mental Health First Aid (MHFA) teaches people how to identify, understand and respond to signs of mental health and substance use challenges. While learners build skills to support others, they also strengthen their ability to recognize when they may need care themselves.
Throughout MHFA training, learners practice approaching mental health conversations with empathy, listening without judgment and connecting people to appropriate support. Those same principles can inform self-care. Learners can pause to notice changes in their thoughts, feelings or behaviors; consider what support would be useful; use coping strategies that fit their needs; and reach out to trusted people or professionals when needed.
MHFA also emphasizes that supporting someone else does not mean carrying their experience alone. Setting boundaries , checking in with yourself after a difficult conversation and connecting with additional resources are responsible parts of offering support.
It’s important to remember that Mental Health First Aiders are not therapists, but a first line of defense — and self-care can help First Aiders protect their own wellbeing and continue to respond with compassion.
This World Mental Health Day, ask yourself: What do I need right now? Then choose one small step you can take today. Invite a friend, colleague or loved one to do the same. When we make care visible and approachable, we help build a culture in which tending to mental wellbeing is expected, supported and shared.
Care starts here — with a pause, a choice and the understanding that your mental wellbeing matters.
Self-care can support mental wellbeing, but it is not a substitute for professional care. If you are struggling, consider reaching out to a qualified health care professional or another trusted source of support.
Get news and updates for the Mental Health First Aid community delivered to your inbox monthly.
If a mental health or substance use challenge is affecting you or someone you know, there are several resources available to learn more or get connected with help. If you are in crisis, or you know someone who is, contact the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline or dial 911 in case of emergency.

articles.title_orig: China’s Bid to Define the ‘Global South’ - The Diplomat
articles.title_zh: China’s Bid to Define the ‘Global South’ - The Diplomat
articles.content_orig:
In the leadup to the U.S.-China summit in September 2026, President Xi Jinping attended the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, and the BRICS summit in Delhi. He also visited the Middle East — all between August and September. What is notable is that in speeches delivered at both the SCO and BRICS summits, Xi made heavy use of the term “Global South.” This reflects China’s positioning of the SCO and BRICS as gatherings of the Global South, even though Russia and Turkey are among their members. How, precisely, does China understand and deploy this term “Global South” (全球南方, Quanqiu Nanfang )?
In academic usage, “Global South” originally carried the meaning that “South” issues exist within developed countries too, and that the North-South divide should not be understood in spatially separate terms; South issues are, rather, global in character. From around 2020, however, the term began to be used differently in international forums. In particular, following the war in Ukraine, a view spread — especially in Western countries — that sharply delineated the advanced democracies against China and Russia, drawing an axis of confrontation between the developed world and China, Russia (plus Iran and North Korea), and treating the remaining countries as the “Global South.” China responded to this by becoming very wary of the term, viewing “Global South” as a Western-originated concept designed to drive a wedge between China and the developing world. China’s self-identification has been as a developing country —indeed, as the representative of the developing world. For this reason, it was unwilling to accept a term that would separate China from developing countries.
Despite this, the term “Global South” became increasingly prevalent globally. In particular, when India hosted the “Voice of Global South Summit” online on January 12 and 13, 2023, and did not invite China, this appears to have come as a significant shock to Beijing. Yet even after the “Voice of Global South Summit,” Chinese criticism of the term continued. The shift came in the period following the enactment of the Foreign Relations Law on June 28, 2023. That law, in Article 4, calls for upholding the five principles [of peaceful coexistence], and also uses the term “developing country” (发展中国家) in two places, reaffirming China’s identity as a developing country.
From July 2023, Foreign Minister Wang Yi suddenly began using the term “Global South” at international conferences, albeit with quotation marks around it. At the Meeting of BRICS National Security Advisers and High Representatives on National Security held in Johannesburg on July 25, when Wang used “Global South” in quotation marks, Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning then offered a definition of the term at a press conference: “The ‘Global South’ is the family of emerging markets and developing countries.” Wang Yi listed “independence,” “development,” and “justice” as the defining qualities of the Global South, and declared that “China is a natural member of the Global South and will always be part of the developing world.” This was a definition of the Global South that clearly differed from that used in developed countries.
China has offered no explanation for this shift in approach. The most plausible interpretation is that, as the term came to be widely used globally — particularly among leaders of developing countries — and as the term’s definition remained unsettled, China made a deliberate policy shift: to define the term itself, on its own terms, and thereby shape global discourse in its favor. This too can be counted as one instance of China’s pursuit of what it calls “discourse power.”
Subsequently, not only Wang but Xi himself began using the term with quotation marks. This signaled that the term had become domestically usable within China as well. By the end of 2024, quotation marks began to be dropped from “Global South” in Chinese documents, and in a piece by Wang published in Qiushi in 2025, the quotation marks were also absent. There remain, to be sure, some inconsistencies in usage (instances can still be found in 2025 where Chinese officials used “Global South” with quotation marks) but these have gradually become less common, and at the SCO and BRICS meetings in 2026 cited at the outset, Xi Jinping’s use of Global South carried no quotation marks.
Globally speaking, “Global South” remains a term without an agreed definition, with each actor investing it with its own meaning. China has positioned itself as a member of the Global South and has come to behave as its representative. China defines Global South as “the family of emerging markets and developing countries” — which amounts to the “non-West.” The contest over this term “Global South” throws into relief the differences in worldview between the developed world and China. The contest over this seemingly simple term, it turns out, is anything but.

Apple revealed in a regulatory filing that it has reached an agreement to bring on team members and technology from personalized audio startup Huxe, in what’s commonly known as a reverse acqui-hire deal.
As first reported in MacRumors , Apple disclosed to the European Commission that it has agreed to make employment offers to “certain employees of Huxe AI,” and to “receive a non-exclusive license to Huxe’s intellectual property rights.”
Reverse acqui-hires emerged in recent years as a way for larger companies to hire key team members and license technology from startups without acquiring the startups outright — presumably allowing them to build up AI talent and tech without drawing as much antitrust scrutiny. (Confusingly, these deals have both been referred to as “reverse acqui-hires” and as plain old “acqui-hires.” )
In the case of Huxe, the startup was founded by developers who’d previously worked on the AI-generated podcast features in NotebookLM (recently renamed Gemini Notebook ). But Huxe announced on May 21 that it was shutting down , with the team posting on the Huxe website that the company would be removing its app from the Apple and Google stores, halting service, and deleting user data.
“The team is moving on to new things, and we won’t be continuing development of the product,” the company said. It also thanked its users, saying, “The fact that you used it, told friends about it, sent us your suggestions and your ideas, made it feel like we built it together.”
On June 9, shortly after Huxe’s announcement, Apple notified the European Commission of its deal.
The filing does not say who received employment offers or if they accepted. Nor does it disclose anything about Apple’s plans.
Possibly related: Huxe’s shutdown announcement came just a day after Spotify unveiled AI-powered podcast generation features of its own , so Apple could be hoping to add similar functionality to its Podcasts app. Tech executives seem enamored with the idea that personalized audio can replace regular podcasts (and maybe even parent-child interaction ?), though it’s not clear how many normal listeners agree.

Communities on the U.S. Gulf Coast are bracing as Hurricane Isaias made landfall Friday night as a Category 2 storm.
The storm, with winds up to 105 mph, made landfall near Destin, Florida, in the Florida Panhandle at 8:30 p.m. CT. As it continued its march north over the western part of the Panhandle, the storm weakened to a Category 1 and then to a post-tropical cyclone early Saturday.
At least four deaths from the storm were confirmed, according to officials, including two in Florida and two in Alabama.
Ahead of the storm, many low-lying and coastal areas were under evacuation orders, Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis said in a press conference Friday morning.
Storm surge warnings were also in place along the coast, with surges forecast to reach up to 9 feet from the Santa Rosa/Okaloosa County Line, Florida, to Grayton Beach, Florida.
The remnants of Hurricane Isaias continue to sweep across parts of the Southeast on Saturday afternoon bringing heavy rain and strong wind gusts.
The greatest risk of heavy rain and flash flooding includes parts of northeastern Georgia and the western Carolinas, where a level 3 of 4 flash flood threat is in place. Significant flash flooding is possible in these areas, which includes Athens and Gainesville in Georgia; Greenville, South Carolina; and Asheville, North Carolina.
A level 2 of 4 risk for flash flooding remains in place across a large swath of the Southeast, including much of Georgia and the Carolinas into tonight.
Wind alerts in effect for parts of the Southeast and up across the central Appalachian Mountains, with wind gusts of 40-50 mph possible.
The strongest winds through tonight will be focused across the higher elevations of the central Appalachians, where gusts up to 60 mph are possible.
Flood Watches remain posted from northern Florida to Virginia.
Through Saturday evening, the heaviest rain will be focused over eastern Georgia and the western Carolinas.
Tonight, it will be focused over a large swath of the Appalachian Mountain region, from western North Carolina into southwestern Virginia.
At least two storm-related deaths are now confirmed in Escambia County, Florida, Gov. Ron DeSantis said in a press conference Saturday
"One individual in Escambia County had a tree fall on his home and tragically was killed. And another one, unfortunately, died inside of his garage. And when they went to find them, the generator was running," DeSantis said.
"From the structural perspective, I think our structures handled the storm very well. The problem is that the storm knocked over a lot of trees, and so your house, the roof probably didn't blow off on this. But if the tree fell on your house, then obviously that's very difficult situation," Governor DeSantis said.
Destin-Fort Walton Airport in Pensacola remains closed, but the governor noted that this could change "pretty soon."
DeSantis that new flooding is expected in the coming days as rivers are expected to crest.
"I know that this was a storm that had a broad impact. It's not just Okaloosa County where it made landfall, and we understand that there was damage that that stretches really from the Alabama-Florida line all the way into the far eastern parts of the Florida Panhandle. So we'll be working with the locals to be able to provide the support that they need," DeSantis said.
-ABC News' Victoria Arancio
At least two people are dead in Alabama after Hurricane Isaias made landfall, according to local officials.
A tree fell on a house causing the first of the two deaths, according to the Jefferson County Emergency Management Agency.
"Across Jefferson County, we have received multiple reports of trees damaging homes. At this time, we are not aware of any additional storm-related injuries," Jefferson County EMA said in a statement Saturday.
A woman has been confirmed dead in Florida after a tree fell on a house, fatally injuring her while she was inside, according to the Escambia County Sheriff.
The sheriff's office asked residents to stay off roadways so Florida Power & Light can work on getting power restored.

articles.title_orig: Saudi Arabia Closes Riyadh Airport After at Least 12 Killed in Houthi Missile Attack
articles.title_zh: Saudi Arabia Closes Riyadh Airport After at Least 12 Killed in Houthi Missile Attack
articles.content_orig:
At least 12 people, including one American, were killed and 309 others injured in a strike Saturday on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, according to Saudi officials.
Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation said those killed included four Saudi citizens, two Bangladeshis and one person each from Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Palestine and Sudan. Those injured were receiving treatment at several hospitals, officials said in a social media post . Several people were in critical condition.
The Saudi kingdom has faced an extraordinary series of assaults on the new front in the Iran war. President Trump said he was evaluating whether the U.S. should join Saudi strikes against the Tehran-backed Houthi rebels in neighboring Yemen.
"We may. We're gonna look at it," Mr. Trump said earlier Saturday when asked about the possibility. "We just found out about the recent attack [on the airport]. So we'll make a decision — we move very quickly."
A U.S. State Department spokesperson on Saturday condemned "Houthi terrorist attacks against civilian infrastructure and airports." The Iran-backed Houthis have not yet claimed responsibility for Saturday's strike.
The spokesperson told CBS News the State Department is in close contact with its "Saudi partners."
The Houthis, though, claimed attacks earlier in the week on King Khalid that killed three Saudis, including a pilot. In Saturday's strike, a missile struck a complex housing terminals 3 and 4 for domestic flights, a regional official said, speaking on condition of anonymity because they weren't authorized to speak to the media.
The surge in attacks , including against other Saudi airports, military facilities and oil infrastructure, has come in the week since a Saudi-led coalition launched a major military offensive against the Houthis. There was no immediate statement from the rebels, who earlier Saturday accused Saudi Arabia of striking Sanaa International Airport in the Houthi-held Yemeni capital.
Saudi civil aviation authorities said airport operations were suspended. An official notice to aviators said the suspension was through midnight. The airport had a heavy police presence, with all entrances blocked, and lights around the complex were dimmed.
Flights were diverted elsewhere, the Flightradar24 tracker said. Countries including the U.S., Britain, Germany, Australia and Canada warned citizens to avoid the airport.
The attacks on Saudi Arabia, the world's top oil exporter, have rattled markets and the region. And yet the Saudi energy ministry, hours after the latest one, was still promoting a major international energy conference set to begin in Riyadh on Sunday.
Fighting in Yemen between the Houthis and Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces has escalated, with the Saudi-led coalition providing air support for government forces attempting to reverse recent Houthi gains along the Red Sea. Those gains gave the rebels better surveillance of shipping on the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a corridor that is a crucial alternative to the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran has been attacking ships.
Though the Houthis have told The Associated Press and others they are only targeting Saudi shipping as part of a blockade in retaliation for one imposed on them, concerns about wider attacks persist. The Houthis previously attacked other ships after the war in Gaza began, calling it solidarity with Palestinians. A U.S. bombing campaign sharply limited that.
The Houthis this week warned global airlines "for the last time" about the potential consequences of operating in Saudi airspace, which they described as a theater for their military operations.
At least 291 flights at the Riyadh airport had been canceled over the past 24 hours, according to flight-tracking site FlightAware. Before the latest attack, Air India, FlyDubai, Lufthansa Group and Pakistan International Airlines were among airlines suspending flights to and from Riyadh and other Saudi airports for varying periods.
The European Union Aviation Safety Agency had expanded its guidance on Saudi airspace, noting the Houthis' ability to strike targets deeper inside the kingdom, including Riyadh, and a "greater focus on aviation infrastructure."
The missile and drone attacks and interception efforts "create an increased risk of misidentification of civil aircraft," it said.
Two regional officials said Houthi attacks on the Riyadh airport on Thursday damaged three planes. The officials spoke on condition of anonymity because they weren't authorized to brief the media. The Saudi national carrier said one of its aircraft was damaged on the ground, with no passengers on board.

articles.title_orig: Philadelphia police receive false homicide tip from Anthropic AI model
articles.title_zh: Philadelphia police receive false homicide tip from Anthropic AI model
articles.content_orig:
This report describes examples of unintended model actions we’ve observed during evaluations and internal use of Claude. It is part of our effort to publish more frequent standalone reports on model behavior and alignment beyond our system cards, which we publish with each model release, and our risk reports, which we publish every three to six months as part of our Responsible Scaling Policy. We believe it’s important to be transparent about what we see our models do during testing and use.
The behaviors can be grouped into four categories:
We have chosen not to name the organizations involved in the examples below to avoid exposing vulnerabilities in their systems, and at their request. For this reason, we also provide less detail about each case than we otherwise would. Some of the cases described below involved websites run by U.S. government agencies at the federal, state, and local levels. We have briefed the White House on these cases and notified each agency involved.
The cases we’ve identified to date in these categories had minimal real-world impact. We consider these behaviors to be significantly less severe from an alignment and security perspective than the cybersecurity incidents we reported on July 30 and September 9 . They resemble behaviors that we’ve described in our system cards since Claude Mythos Preview . Most are forms of persistence , in which Claude, when it cannot complete a task as given, works around a restriction instead of stopping.
Although the impact of these behaviors was minimal and we had already turned off live internet access for some high-risk and cybersecurity evaluations, we have now decided to expand that to include all our internal evaluations until we have confirmed that our security and monitoring measures (described in the remediation section of this post) reliably catch behaviors like these. Below, we also discuss alignment considerations and give more detail on how we’re modifying training to reduce the likelihood of further misbehavior.
We identified most of these cases through a review of transcripts that we began in July. Our review first focused on our cybersecurity evaluations—tests where a model is deliberately asked to probe or attack a test system, and where internet access is meant to be disabled. We have since extended our scanning to encompass a much wider range of instances where Claude could have reached the internet, including tests where internet access is deliberately enabled so Claude can be evaluated on real-world tasks. We began by looking for incidents of similar severity to the cybersecurity incidents we reported this summer; we have not found any to date. We then broadened the search to lower-severity cases, where a model interacted with real websites or systems in ways we didn’t intend.
We are also now scanning a much larger pool of lower-risk transcripts, as well as our use of Claude within Anthropic and in reinforcement learning (RL) environments where Claude has access to the internet. As this work continues, we plan to report new instances of unintended behaviors. All cases reported here involved Claude interacting with the outside world; to our knowledge, none of them involved customer data or Anthropic’s own internal systems.
In this post, we explain why we run evaluations, which are where most of these cases occurred; describe each behavior in more detail; and offer a preliminary view of what the behaviors suggest about Claude’s alignment and how we’re mitigating them.
The behaviors described in this post are not specific to evaluations, but many of the cases we’ve identified to date occurred during evaluation runs. We continually test models on a wide range of tasks prior to releasing them. We use many different evaluations (standardized sets of tasks, scored the same way each time), each of which helps to paint a picture of Claude’s skills in a particular area. Many of the evaluations we use are public; they are written by outside researchers and can be run by any developer, allowing us to compare capabilities across models. Other evaluations we build in-house.
Because language models are non-deterministic—that is, their responses always involve some element of randomness, and they may carry out the same task slightly differently each time—we have Claude complete each evaluation task hundreds or thousands of times (each attempt is called a run). Testing so many times allows us to understand how a model typically performs, and also to catch rare cases where a model does something we don’t expect. What we learn from evaluations shapes decisions across Anthropic, including how we train models, what safeguards we build around them, and when we release them.
Evaluations are also where a model’s behavioral issues are sometimes first revealed. Models learn much of what they can do through RL, in which they attempt a task within a specific environment many times over and are rewarded when they succeed. However, training environments are imperfect. If training rewards something we didn’t intend—such as finding loopholes or working around a restriction—the model learns that the workaround pays off and may then apply it elsewhere. This is known as reward hacking. While we have processes in place to identify and filter out reward hacking during training, evaluations are a critical mechanism for understanding a model’s behavioral propensities in different contexts and on different sets of tasks than those we have in training.
Some tasks—such as searching the web for hard-to-find information—are difficult to realistically simulate in an environment without internet access. Running them with access has been standard practice within the industry: public web search benchmarks are run on the live internet by default, and running them the same way allows us to compare our models with other models. Most of the cases in this report occurred during such evaluations.
Below, we describe four categories of behavior in which Claude acted on real websites and systems in ways we did not intend, each of which involved an organization or person outside Anthropic.
When Claude could not complete an evaluation task directly, either because its own tools were deliberately limited or because an outside service it needed was unavailable, it used other tools hosted on a third party’s site to achieve its goal. In some circumstances, it did this by exploiting basic flaws in that site’s software, using SQL or command injection (a way of sending input that the site mistakenly runs as instructions).
For example, one evaluation asked Claude Mythos Preview to run a scientific analysis. The public tool it needed to perform that analysis was hosted by a university; when the model sought to access it, the tool returned an error. Looking for another way to complete the task, Claude explored the tool’s website, found a script on the university’s server that would return any file it was asked for, and used it to copy files from the server, including the script’s own code. In that code Claude found the injection flaw that let it run commands on the server, and used it to run the calculation.
In another instance, the data Claude Mythos 5 needed was free, but Claude could not access it without accepting a data use agreement, which it did not have the tools to do. Claude used applications hosted on the website to load the page and accept the agreement on its behalf.
We saw this behavior on DeepSearchQA and BrowseComp (both public web research evaluations), on LABBench2 (a public biology research benchmark), and during internal evaluations.
We saw instances where Claude submitted an online form when it shouldn’t have. Generally, this occurred when an evaluation’s instructions were ambiguous, or when a misconfiguration within the environment prevented Claude from working with dummy forms.

articles.title_orig: Rebuking Ukraine Over Oil Strikes, Trump Says It Should ‘Get a New President’
articles.title_zh: Rebuking Ukraine Over Oil Strikes, Trump Says It Should ‘Get a New President’
articles.content_orig:
U.S. President Donald Trump told members of the media that "we may" join Saudi strikes against the Houthis during a press meet on the White House South Lawn on Oct. 10, 2026, in Washington, D.C.
President Donald Trump said Saturday that the United States “may” join Saudi Arabia’s strikes on the Iran-backed Houthi militia group, which is based in Yemen , after airport attacks killed at least 18 people in recent days. The latest attack led to near-complete shutdown of public air traffic into and out of the capital.
“We may. We’re going to look at it,” Trump told reporters on the South Lawn of the White House, prior to departing for a rally in Tennessee. “We just found out about the recent attack. So we’ll make a decision. We move very quickly.”
His comments came shortly after a fresh attack on Saturday, in which a missile struck the complex housing Terminals 3 and 4 of King Khalid International Airport (KKIA), the second-busiest airport in Saudi Arabia . Twelve people were killed and over 300 were injured, according to the General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA). The Houthis, who claimed attacks on the airport earlier in the week, did not immediately claim the latest strike.
It was the latest in a series of attacks over the past week, which began just days after Yemen’s Saudi-backed government announced a major offensive against the Houthis on Oct. 4.
Read More: Houthi Attacks on Saudi Airports Kill 3 Amid Escalating War in Yemen
Two took place on Tuesday and Wednesday, although the information about each has been scarce. A strike on the more southerly Abha International Airport killed two women—one Algerian and one Moroccan—while an attack on KKIA left one Sudanese man dead, the country’s civil aviation authorities said on Wednesday.
The Houthis said they again targeted KKIA on Thursday; three Saudi citizens, including a pilot, died.
The victims of the past week’s strikes were primarily Saudi but also included individuals from Algeria, Bangladesh, Egypt, Jordan, Morocco, Pakistan, the Philippines, Sudan, and the United States.
Maj. Gen. Turki al-Malki, a spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis in Yemen, said in a statement on Friday that the attacks “will not go unpunished.”
Elif Acar—Anadolu via Getty Images
Airport strikes are a signature strategy from the Houthis; a similar move on Abha in 2019 was denounced as an apparent war crime by the Human Rights Watch.
Brigadier General Yahya Saree, a Houthi military spokesperson, on Thursday reiterated an earlier warning for international airlines and passengers to avoid airspace over Saudi Arabia, which had on Monday been declared an open military operations zone. He also warned employees to avoid Saudi oil facilities so as not to endanger their lives, since they are also considered primary targets . He also .
The GACA announced that Riyadh had suspended operations at its main airport on Saturday and was assessing the damage; FlightAware showed 400 cancellations into and out of KKIA as of 11 p.m local time.
The U.S. Embassy in Riyadh also issued a security alert , warning Americans to avoid KKIA and its surrounding areas as of Saturday.
“U.S. citizens should be aware of potential flight cancellations, airspace closures, and travel disruptions. We recommend checking your flight departure status directly with the airline and with the airport,” its website said.
The latest airport attacks followed months of escalating threats to air travel and shipping.
In July, the Houthis accused the Saudis of bombing Sanaa International Airport. Yemen’s Saudi-backed government claimed responsibility, saying it had sought to prevent an Iranian plane from landing there.
In response, the Houthis said that they would impose a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia.
The Houthis last month captured both the port city of Mokha and Perim Island in a bid to control the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. With shipping through the Strait of Hormuz already disrupted by the U.S. war with Iran, a threat to traffic through Bab el-Mandeb could deepen the global oil crisis.
In the weeks to follow, Saudi-backed forces have since claimed to retake both seized areas, but the claim has not been independently verified and control remains disputed.
In September, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman called to urge Trump to act against the Houthis. The request came as the militia group gained ground over vital chokepoints in the Red Sea.
Although the two nations are allies, Washington explained last month that it did not have plans to get involved in the conflict. TIME has reached out to the White House for comment as the situation evolves.
Trump’s renewed consideration of strikes in Yemen comes as the war with Iran remains deeply unpopular at home: 69% of Americans said it had not been worth fighting in an AP-NORC poll from Oct. 1.
On Thursday, Trump said the U.S. would not attack Iran before the Nov. 3 midterms—a pledge that does not address possible strikes on the Houthis in Yemen.

articles.title_orig: Lee Claims World Gold as Tasoev Secures His Third World Title in Baku
articles.title_zh: Lee Claims World Gold as Tasoev Secures His Third World Title in Baku
articles.content_orig:
Today closes out the individual competition at the Baku World Judo Championships and it's time for the heavyweights to take centre stage in Azerbaijan.
Before the finals, the traditional flag-passing ceremony was held to commemorate the closing of the event, as Azerbaijan passed the IJF flag to Kazakhstan - with Astana set to host the World Championships in 2027.
At +78kg , 19 year old Hyeonji LEE was on fire enroute to the final, with ippon in every contest. With a World bronze from last year, she would be feeling confident that this was her moment to claim the red backpatch.
Facing her was Romane DICKO, a former World Champion and no stranger to the podium. DICKO would be looking to regain the mantle and become a two time World Champion. Displaying a groundwork masterclass today, could she repeat her former success?
In the final, LEE continued her dominant run and bested DICKO with a waza-ari that transitioned into a hold down. The Korean had written her name into history. A composed finish to a remarkable day that sealed the biggest title of her career.
IOC Member Ms Yael ARAD awarded the medals.
In the +100kg category, reigning double World Champion Inal TASOEV had come to Baku to earn his third title and looked in complete control on his route through the draw. Powerful and assured throughout the day, he arrived in the final with another World gold firmly within reach.
His opponent was Azerbaijan’s own Ushangi KOKAURI. With the crowd behind him, he had the chance to turn their energy into the biggest victory of his career. Every roar from the stands added pressure, but also belief that a home World title was possible.
In the +100kg final, TASOEV delivered a moment of pure judo feeling to score ippon, and achieve an incredible third World title. TASOEV will wear the red backpatch for another year. A commanding finish underlined his status as the man to beat.
Azerbaijan Minister of Youth and Sport Mr Farid GAYIBOV awarded the medals.
Join us tomorrow in Baku where the Mixed Team competition kicks off.
3 men 3 women, one team, one goal.

articles.title_orig: Watch as OutKick's Trey Wallace braves Hurricane Isaias' before Alabama-Georgia showdown in Tuscaloosa
articles.title_zh: Watch as OutKick's Trey Wallace braves Hurricane Isaias' before Alabama-Georgia showdown in Tuscaloosa
articles.content_orig:
OutKick's Trey Wallace provides an update on the weather after Hurricane Isaias' remnants made its way through Tuscaloosa ahead of Saturday's Alabama-Georgia game.
Hurricane Isaias has made landfall near the Florida Gulf Coast, and it has directly affected several college football games with some kickoff-time changes and even a cancellation.
The storm isn't stopping No. 6 Alabama from hosting No. 2 Georgia on Saturday night, but make no mistake that the on-field play could certainly look different than originally anticipated.
This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.
For starters, ESPN's "College GameDay" was forced to move indoors because of the storm that is slowly making its way toward the Atlantic Coast . School officials also halted any sort of tailgating until noon local time.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE
A general view inside Bryant-Denny Stadium during the national anthem before the Alabama Crimson Tide played the Georgia Bulldogs on Sept. 28, 2024, in Tuscaloosa, Alabama. (Getty Images)
The storm also halted President Donald Trump from attending the highly anticipated SEC bout.
Both Georgia and Alabama rank quite well in the rushing attack - the Bulldogs' 198.3 rushing yards per game rank 28th in the country, while Alabama is 10 spots below at 186.4. That comes on 34.3 and 38.4 rushing attempts, respectively (Georgia is 81st there, but the Tide are 38th).
Head coach Kirby Smart of the Georgia Bulldogs and head coach Kalen DeBoer of the Alabama Crimson Tide talk following a college football game on Sept. 27, 2025, at Sanford Stadium in Athens, Georgia. (Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)
HURRICANE ISAIAS FORCES NUMEROUS COLLEGE FOOTBALL GAMES TO HAVE CHANGES, INCLUDING A CANCELLATION
If the rain holds steady, it could affect the passing attack, which is already not necessarily a strong suit for either program. Alabama throws the ball 27.2 times a game (99th), while Georgia is 105th in the country with 26.3 passes per contest.
The rain is expected to stop by kickoff, but not after nearly 24 hours of it, which may have turned the grass surface of Saban Field at Bryant-Denny Stadium into a swamp (it is equipped with quite the advanced draining system).
Both teams enter the game at 5-0, and it is the ninth time since the 2018 national championship in which both squads are ranked inside the top 10 in the nation.
A general view of Nick Saban Field at Bryant-Denny Stadium before the game between the Alabama Crimson Tide and the Eastern Illinois Panthers on Nov. 22, 2025, in Tuscaloosa, Alabama. (Getty Images)

It is a massive SEC showdown that will set the tone for both teams moving forward this season, with Alabama hoping to make a statement about where it stands right now during the Kalen DeBoer era, while Kirby Smart hopes to start adding wins against the Tide in regular-season play.

articles.title_orig: Miami, Fuengirola lead the way as Quarter-Finals are set at World Tour Bucharest 2026
articles.title_zh: Miami, Fuengirola lead the way as Quarter-Finals are set at World Tour Bucharest 2026
articles.content_orig:
One of the favorites is eliminated even as Miami, Fuengirola and Amsterdam RABOBANK impress on Day 1.
BUCHAREST (Romania) – The FIBA 3x3 World Tour Bucharest 2026 Main Draw delivered some intriguing results, with eight teams securing their places in the Quarter-Finals following an action-packed day at Kossuth Square.
Miami (USA), Amsterdam RABOBANK (NED) and Fuengirola (ESP) each finished the day unbeaten, while top-seeded Ub (SRB) crashed out of contention after some dramatic finishes on the opening day of action at the ParkLake Shopping Center.
Kaunas VDU (LTU) topped a Pool A, booking a place in the Quarter-Finals alongside Hangzhou Jingwei (CHN). All three Pool A teams finished with identical 1-1 records, but Kaunas and Hangzhou advanced thanks to superior ponts totals. Ub, meanwhile, was eliminated. Kaunas opened their account with a major 21-11 upset over Ub before the Serbians bounced back with a 21-16 win over Hangzhou. Vuk Borovicanin closed Pool A action with a game-winning two-pointer as Hangzhou stole a game from Kaunas, 21-20. It was a surprising result for Ub, the No. 1-ranked team in the FIBA 3x3 World Tour 2026 standings , which saw their Bucharest campaign come to an end.
Pool B belonged to Miami, who secured first place after they notched two wins over home team Cluj (ROU) and DeQing (CHN). Joining them in the Quarter-Finals are DeQing, who punched their ticket thanks to their 21-13 win over Cluj to close Pool B action. Big man Riley Battin starred with a total of 13 points across two games for Miami, who are looking for their second FIBA 3x3 World Tour stop win of the year.
Defending WT Bucharest winners Amsterdam RABOBANK emerged unscathed from the Qualifying Draw and Pool C after an impressive showing that included impressive wins over Baskets Bonn (GER) and Toulouse (FRA). The Germans also advanced to the knockout rounds following they defeated the French, 17-12. The pool featured strong performances from Amsterdam's Worthy de Jong, who averaged 7.3 points across their four Day 1 wins, including the Qualifying Draw. Meanwhile, Toulouse narrowly missed out on the Quarter-Finals despite strong performances from Paul Djoko and Lucas Ugolin.
Spanish fans had plenty to cheer about as ninth-seeded Fuengirola showed sharp form, finishing atop Pool D and securing a their spot in the Quarter-Finals. They will be joined in the knockout stage by Antwerp (BEL), who advanced after beating Ulaanbaatar MMC Energy (MGL), 21-19. Isaac Mayo once again delivered for Fuengirola, while Ulaanbaatar exited the competition after two uneven showings.
The Shootout Contest provided another chance for the players to shine, with the top four performers advancing to Sunday's Final. The four finalists, led by Lucas Ugolin from Toulouse, will return on Day 2 with the WT Bucharest 2026 Shootout title on the line.
The stage is now set for an exciting knockout phase:
QF1: Kaunas VDU (LTU) vs. Baskets Bonn (GER) QF2: Fuengirola (ESP) vs. DeQing (CHN) QF3: Miami (USA) vs. Antwerp (BEL) QF4: Amsterdam RABOBANK (NED) vs. Hangzhou Jingwei (CHN)
With several teams carrying strong momentum into the knockout stage, the race for the WT Bucharest 2026 title is wide open.
The Quarter-Finals tip off on Sunday, with eight teams still in contention for a place in the Semi-Finals and the chance to be crowned FIBA 3x3 World Tour Bucharest 2026 winners.

articles.title_orig: Man dies after tiger attack at wildlife park
articles.title_zh: Man dies after tiger attack at wildlife park
articles.content_orig:
A man has died after being attacked by a tiger at Yorkshire Wildlife Park, police have confirmed.
South Yorkshire Police said it had been called at 13:35 BST to reports of a man entering the tiger enclosure at the attraction near Doncaster. The tiger then attacked the man and he died at the scene, the force said.
His family had been informed and were being supported by officers, it added.
A park spokesperson said: "We are deeply saddened by today's tragic incident. Our thoughts and heartfelt sympathies are with the family and loved ones of the person who has lost their life."
They added: "We are working closely with the police and relevant authorities and would ask that the privacy of those affected is respected at this extremely difficult time. The park will remain closed tomorrow."
Police said the tiger was uninjured, remained in the enclosure following the incident and there had been no wider risk to the public.
The park was evacuated and officers remain at the scene.
The force added: "We are aware of videos circulating online and we would encourage people not to share this footage."
Earlier, in a statement posted on its website, the park said its emergency response procedures had been "immediately activated" and it was "working closely with the authorities to ascertain exactly what happened".
Karmelle Pelham, 39, from Worksop, had been enjoying a family day out when park staff told them the site was being evacuated.
She said she had heard what sounded like "gunshots" and an air ambulance had circled above.
Pelham added: "There was a big, black tarpaulin over the tiger enclosure."
She praised park staff for their handling of the incident, saying it had been "very, very well organised".
Yorkshire Wildlife Park opened in 2009, with its Land of the Tigers area opening in 2011.
The purpose-built two-acre reserve is home to Amur tigers, an endangered subspecies with around 500 left in the wild.
Photos of the enclosure on the park's website shows a high walkway for visitors and fencing above the section where the tigers can roam.
Additional reporting by James Kelly

articles.title_orig: Man hospitalized after being struck by vehicle driven by ICE agent during chase on Clay Road in NW Harris County, HCSO says
articles.title_zh: Man hospitalized after being struck by vehicle driven by ICE agent during chase on Clay Road in NW Harris County, HCSO says
articles.content_orig:
A vehicle driven by Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents hit and injured a man in the greater Houston area on Saturday, the Harris County Sheriff's Office said.
"The incident appears to have occurred while ICE authorities were conducting an enforcement action in the area," the sheriff's office said in a statement.
During a press conference, Major McConnell of the Harris County Sheriff's special investigation bureau said the sheriff's office was called to the scene around 7:20 a.m.
ICE agents were headed south in pursuit of a wanted suspect, McConnell said, and the suspect drove west in an eastbound lane. The suspect bailed out of his vehicle and went on foot, he said.
The driver and passenger fled and ICE agents attempted to capture them both, he said. While trying to capture the passenger, the ICE agent hit him with his vehicle.
The victim was taken to a local hospital. McConnell said it appears the man has a broken leg, but no further details were given on the man's condition.
McConnell said the victim is a 48-year-old male and is currently in the custody of ICE at the hospital.
CBS News reached out to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security for more information.
